title: Training Q&A: Lapse Rate on Builder-Delay Waivers, Builder Extended Rate Lock
content:
**Q: When does a lapse rate reduce a builder-delay waiver on a Builder Extended Rate Lock?**
A: The lapse gap is the calendar days from the buyer's latest closing date notice from Calloway to the lock's expired date. On a relocked lock whose lapse gap is above 7 days, the lapse rate is 0.5; on a relocked lock whose lapse gap is one day up to 7 days, it is 0.8; otherwise it is one.

**Q: How is the lapse rate used?**
A: The waiver percent of the extension charge is multiplied by the lapse rate before the result is rounded half up to the cent.

**Q: What makes a lock a relocked lock here?**
A: Its lock ledger carries a relock fee charge.

**Q: Where do the dates come from?**
A: The closing date notice is the latest closing date notice on the Home Purchase Agreement ledger of the agreement the lock finances; the expired date is the one on the lock record.

**Q: What are the rates at a glance?**

| Relocked lock | Lapse gap | Lapse rate |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | 8 days or more | 0.5 |
| Yes | 1 to 7 days | 0.8 |
| Yes | none, or the expired date not after the notice | 1 |
| No | any | 1 |

**Q (hypothetical): latest closing date notice 3 June, expired date 10 June, relocked lock, extension charge USD 600.00 at a waiver percent of 100?**
A: Gap 7 days, lapse rate 0.8: 600.00 multiplied by 0.8 is USD 480.00. With an expired date of 11 June the gap is 8 days and the lapse rate 0.5, giving USD 300.00.
